To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BOLD signal in the ventral striatum (VS) correlates with a reward prediction error (RPE) that is modulated by experienced reward variance (risk).
the neural signals of reward prediction error in the ventral striatum reflect a risk-sensitive learning process that is closely coupled to the experience-based evaluations that guide human choice.

(1) the BOLD signal in the nucleus accubens correlates with the prediction errors that are the basis of the reinforcement-learning model of animal learning; (2) the BOLD prediction-error signal is also sensitive to the risk associated with rewards; (3) this risk-sensitive BOLD signal correlates with the risk-sensitive value function that is the basis of human risk aversion; and (4) the neural risk sensitivity is consistent with the risk sensitivity of the behavioral value function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms underlying risk-sensitive decision making.
the neural basis of risk sensitivity in human reinforcement learning, and the results are consistent with the view that humans and animals learn about risk as well as reward.
how humans and animals learn about the consequences of their actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human brain is risk sensitive, and the neural mechanisms of risk sensitivity have been identified.
risk is an intrinsic part of human learning and that this is reflected by a risk-sensitive prediction error signal in the brain.
the brain uses risk-sensitive reinforcement learning to make optimal choices in a changing world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
risk sensitivity is an integral aspect of human learning, and this is evident from the fact that our brain learns about the variance in the reward values of the stimuli.
the neural prediction error signal is a risk-sensitive reinforcement learning signal.
risk sensitivity is a fundamental property of human learning, and that the brain is equipped with neural mechanisms for learning about risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural signals in the human brain are sensitive to the risk of outcomes.
the neural correlates of reinforcement learning are sensitive not only to the expected reward of an action but also to the risk of the reward.
the brain’s learning system is sensitive to higher moments of the reward distributions and is able to use this information to make decisions that reflect a risk-sensitive policy.
